approvedDesign.title: Hunted A: a neutral follower stays within 4 tiles of the squad and takes the hostile side in the first fight that opens near it while the squad in that fight averages under 70% HP, until the squad withdraws
approvedDesign.problem: Hunted rolls on every type except duel (missiontypes.js:829, weight 8, pays x1.4) and nothing reads it: the id appears in no other .js file. The tag says something follows the squad and joins whichever fight is going worst. No actor follows the squad: a hostile moves only when it sees the squad, remembers it for GIVE_UP = 20 s (field.js:62) or is inside an alarm (chooseGoals, field.js:709). No fight gains a body after it opens: openSkirmish resolves the whole fight once, up front (field.js:1220). The first version of this proposal made the follower an ordinary hostile that trails the squad. Measured on the real harness that version mostly produced run-ins: 2478 fights involved the follower and 317 were joins; the rest were the squad walking into it, a healthy squad could kill it and end the twist, and the effect was an elite standing on the way out. The premise of that version was also wrong. Where baseline deaths happen, 1800 contracts at levels 1-4 (test/sortie.harness.js, 15 types): 126 before the squad began leaving, 54 after the job was done (leave(), field.js:1882) and 524 after a withdrawal (withdraw(), field.js:382, called by broken(), by a lost fight or by the retreat order). Three quarters of deaths are on a walk out that began because the squad was losing, so the walk out is not unthreatened, and a twist that is active there makes the retreat order worth less than it is.
evidence: missiontypes.js:829-830 hunted row (weight 8, x1.4, not duel and arena); no other .js file mentions the id. "arena" is a map id, not a type.

field.js:709 chooseGoals (hostile loop) and :62 GIVE_UP: a hostile moves only on sight, memory or alarm. field.js:55 ENGAGE = 2: a fight is the transitive group of combatants within 2 tiles (findSkirmishes :1198).

field.js:1186 combatant() returns false for structures, civilians, prizes, an actor inside noFightUntil and a ward with a squad member within 1 tile; findSkirmishes (:1198) builds groups only from combatants, so an actor refused here is in no fight however close it stands.

field.js:1220 openSkirmish calls s.resolve(ours, theirs) once before the fight record exists; sortie.js:155-158 resolve builds fighters from exactly those two lists, so a body pushed into `theirs` at that point fights from the first tick and a body left out is not in the fight.

field.js:1695 makeActor already maps a group side "neutral" to actor side "neutral"; no cast group uses it. Every reader of hostiles filters by isTheirs() or side === "theirs": chooseGoals enemies (:767), rally (:820), taskGoal kill (:528), the escort guard `closing` (:722), look() spotting (:849), holdGround (:1849), sortie.js:263 and :1516, and tactics.js:209, :230, :250, :305. A neutral actor is outside all of them without a per-site check. The `!isOurs` tests (field.js:395 pullOut, :508 destroy targets by kind, :1924 leave) also skip it: it is not extracted with the squad and is not a destroy target.

field.js:918 hpOf (mean hp/maxHp) and field.js:1015 escapeHatch: bad = (down > 0 && avg < 0.7) || avg < ESCAPE_HP || ... . The join reads the same function and the same 0.7, without the "someone down" clause.

field.js:1477 contacted() = fights > 0 or any actor spotted. look() (:849) marks spotted only for isTheirs actors, so a trailing neutral follower neither closes the free call-off nor counts as a sighting.

field.js:382 withdraw(s, why, ordered) sets s.withdrew and phase "leaving" for broken(), a lost fight and the retreat order alike; field.js:1487 retreat(s) is refused only when s.withdrew is already set or the run has a result; verdict() reads the terms before the withdrawal flag ("a squad that withdrew but met the terms has completed the job"), so an order given after the terms are met costs the contract nothing.

field.js:1374 (window shut) and :1581 (escalate) re-spawn every hostile and patrol group in map.spawns at 30% and 50% with no check for deferred groups; the follower's group is role "hostile" (pursuit-twist-plumbing skips groups with forTwist).

mapgen.js:45 TEMPORAL, :233 zoneNames, :325-340 build(): an `at` in TEMPORAL gets no zone and its spawn group is marked deferred; field.js start (:2096) places only non-deferred groups. field.js:1727 arrivals() already releases deferred groups on a cue (cued("last-wave")).
field.js:1784 descend() keeps `carried = actors.filter(isOurs)` (:1793): hostiles, neutral actors included, stay on the old floor.

sortie.js:23 REGEN = 0.005 and :511: every actor with a fighter regains 0.5% of max HP per in-game second while not engaged, so 60 s of walking moves a squad from 70% to 100%. No resupply (sortie.js:508) removes it. sortie.js:183: in-fight healing and potions are already in a.fighter.hp when the fight ends.

Measured with test/sortie.harness.js on a scratch copy of the project (snapshot 03:42; later field.js/sortie.js changes add only the contacted/retreat plumbing): twist pinned, no other twist, 15 types (duel excluded), gearless squads of 4 from a 24-character pool (3-5 stars), levels 1-4 cycled, seeds 1-3, same seeds in every arm. Prototype: C:\Users\mersi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha\bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109\scratchpad\pursuit\patch_h.js + patch_h3.js + patch_harness.js on C:\Users\mersi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha\bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109\scratchpad\pursuit\p3 (variants with the withdrawal gate, retreat policy, floors and counters on p5); job lists jobs_h1.txt, h2, c, d, e, f, g, i; results out\*.json; analysis an.js and cmp.js.
approvedDesign.change:
MODS (missiontypes.js:829, on top of u-honesty): hunted: { label: "Hunted", weight: 8, reward: 1.15, not: ["duel"], trial: false, mods: { follower: { keep: 4, lead: 8, reach: 8, joinHp: 0.7, afterWithdraw: false } }, spawn: (lv) => ({ role: "hostile", side: "neutral", grade: "elite", count: 1, at: "trail" }) }. No levelOffset: the follower is fielded at the level the contract's own elites have (contract level + 1, sortie.js GRADE_BUMP).
MOD_TEXT.follower(mods, mission): "One elite-tier hostile, level N (the contract level plus 1), appears when the squad is 8 tiles from the entry and then stays within 4 tiles of the nearest squad member. It takes no part in any fight and cannot be fought, until a fight opens within 8 tiles of it in which the squad members average under 70% HP. It does not join once the squad is withdrawing (its own break-off, a lost fight or a retreat order). When it joins, it fights on the hostile side for the rest of the run."

CONSUMERS (the spawn hook, trial filter, stale-offer rule, card hostile count, respawn-loop skip and planning-zone species list are pursuit-twist-plumbing).
1) missiontypes.js: the row and MOD_TEXT.follower above.
2) mapgen.js:45: add "trail" to TEMPORAL. zoneNames (:233) then makes no zone for it and build() (:340) marks the group deferred, so Field.start (:2096) does not place it.
3) field.js arrivals() (:1727): when counters.trailed is unset, a group is cued at "trail", and the mean position of squadOn(s) is mods.follower.lead tiles or more from s.map.entry (dist2): spawnGroup(s, { ...g, points: [s.map.entry], keep: mods.follower.keep }, 1), counters.trailed = s.clock, and one log line "Death Knight (level 8) is following the squad, 4 tiles behind. It joins a fight only if the squad in it averages under 70% HP, and not once the squad is withdrawing."
4) field.js makeActor() (:1687): `keep: g.keep`. ACTOR_KEYS (:1970) gains "keep"; side is already saved. counters.trailed and counters.joined ride with counters.
5) field.js combatant() (:1186): `if (a.side === "neutral") return false;`. This is the only place that keeps the follower out of fights: walking into it opens none.
6) field.js chooseGoals() (:709), before the `enemies` loop: for each alive, unengaged actor with side "neutral" and a `keep`, goal = { kind: "actor", id: nearest squad actor } when dist2 > keep, else null.
7) field.js openSkirmish() (:1220), before s.resolve: recruit. If an alive, unengaged actor with side "neutral" and `keep` exists, a squad actor in `ours` is within mods.follower.reach (8) of it, hpOf(squad actors in ours) < mods.follower.joinHp (0.7), and (mods.follower.afterWithdraw or not s.withdrew): set side "theirs", keep undefined, spotted true, push it into `theirs`, counters.joined++, counters.joinedAt = s.clock, counters.joinedHp = round(100 x hpOf), and one log line "Death Knight (level 8) joins the fight: the squad in it averages 62% HP, under 70%". After that it is an ordinary hostile: breakOut (:1025), kill() (:1255), loot and sortie.js resolve (:155) treat it like any other.
8) field.js descend() (:1784): `delete s.counters.trailed`; a new follower is released on the new floor.
9) sortie.js renderSide (:1516): the tally gets " · 1 following" while a neutral actor is alive, so the token on the map has a number. bestiary.js brief() (:201): the row key and the row carry `follows` (side "neutral"), so the follower is not merged into a same-species row; briefLine (:252) appends "(follows)". sortie.js briefBox (:1056): a tag "follows the squad" on that row, title "joins a fight only if the squad in it averages under 70% HP, until the squad withdraws". fieldview.js drawActors (:213): a 2 px ring in Tokens.RINGS.follower (tokens.js:33, new colour) under any token with side "neutral". Debrief (u-debrief): "Hunted: the follower joined at M:SS with the squad at P% HP" or "Hunted: the follower never joined" from counters.joined.
10) test/contracts.js: the roll yields one forTwist "hunted" group, side "neutral", at "trail", and the same quotas as the roll without the twist; mapgen marks it deferred with no "trail" zone; the follower is released once when the squad is 8 tiles out and stays within 5 tiles of the nearest squad actor over 60 steps; a squad actor standing on its tile opens no fight; at 60% squad HP with a hostile adjacent the next step opens one fight whose `theirs` include the follower (side "theirs", counters.joined 1), at 80% it does not, at more than 8 tiles it does not, and with s.withdrew set it does not; Tactics.closing, taskGoal kill and rally never return it; escalate() and a shut window add no second follower; save/restore keeps side, keep and counters.trailed and does not re-release; descend() re-releases on the new floor; a saved mission with "hunted" and no trail group still plays.

CARD. Tag "Hunted" titled with MOD_TEXT.follower. Brief row: species, level, x1, "follows the squad", HP when the town has met the species (intel applies as for any row). MAP. The follower is drawn as its species sprite with a ring, 4 tiles behind the squad, and counted in the tally; the join line prints the HP that caused it.

MEASURED, default (join gate 0.7, no join once s.withdrew is set, elite tier at the contract's elite level; 20 contracts per type per seed, 900 contracts, the same seeds without the twist as base). Base: win 61.7%, 0.386 deaths per contract. With the twist: win 60.3%, 0.500 deaths (+30%; per seed +0.12 / +0.19 / +0.04); the follower joined in 68 contracts (7.6%): 28 while the squad was still working and 40 after the terms were met, on the walk home. On those 68 contracts the same seeds without the twist had 33 deaths and 43 wins; with it 128 deaths and 30 wins, so a join costs 1.40 deaths. By type, deaths per contract without -> with: recon 0.17 -> 0.68, escort 0.02 -> 0.25, capture 0.13 -> 0.43, assassination 1.43 -> 1.80, rescue 0.13 -> 0.25, pursuit 0.08 -> 0.20; extermination, siege, dungeon, hold, raid and sabotage do not move. Retreat order whenever the squad averages under 70% HP between fights (900 contracts): joins fall to 1% (7), deaths 0.500 -> 0.393 (-21%), wins 60.3% -> 58.8%; against the same order without the twist (0.378) the twist then costs +4%.
Dial under the same gate: elite at level offset -3 (contract level - 2) +13% deaths with joins in 7% of 1800 contracts (R 1.06); offset -1 +24% (R 1.12, 900 contracts); offset 0 +30% (R 1.14). Gate variants at offset -3, 1800 contracts: no join once the phase is "leaving" for any reason (withdrawal or terms met) joins in 3%, +10% (R 1.04); joinHp 0.85 with the withdrawal clause joins in 18%, +18% (R 1.12); joinHp 0.5 without the clause joins in 14%, +15% (R 1.05).
Heavier variant, afterWithdraw: true (join at any time), offset -3, 1800 contracts: win 61.4% -> 60.3%, 0.388 -> 0.533 deaths (+37%; per seed +0.17 / +0.12 / +0.15), joins in 463 contracts (26%), of which 341 after a withdrawal; 0.76 deaths per join; the same retreat order changes deaths only 0.533 -> 0.511 because 437 of 447 joins are then on the walk out (R 1.17). At offset 0 this variant is +74% (R 1.34). Composition under this variant, 900 contracts each: fighter + 2 clerics + ranger joins in 25% of contracts and deaths rise +27% (0.449 -> 0.572); fighter + fighter + barbarian + ranger joins in 34% and +30% (0.532 -> 0.690). Pairs under this variant (900 contracts): over No resupply, which alone is +15% deaths, Hunted adds +43%; over Night, which alone is +0%, +43%; over Hardcore, which alone is +0% in this harness, +37%. Dungeon (180 contracts): one release per run +8% deaths, one release per floor +20%. The first version (follower can be fought, offset -3): win 57.3%, +25% deaths, 317 joins in 2478 follower fights. Levels 5-8 (1080 contracts; gearless squads win 14.8% and lose 1.25 characters per contract at baseline): +43% deaths, joins in 58%; the harness there measures the squad's incapacity, so no price is taken from it.

MULTIPLIER x1.15 (was x1.4). Rule: the multiplier R that leaves expected gems per contract unchanged, R = (P0 + (d1 - d0) x C) / P1, P the mean pay earned per contract (a win earns (25 + 30 x level) x type multiplier, a loss 0), d deaths per contract, C = 100 gems, the summon price (game.js:8 PULL_COST). Default, levels 1-4: P0/P1 = 1.024, (0.500 - 0.386) x 100 / P1 = 0.121, R = 1.144, rounded up to the next 0.05 = 1.15. With a death valued at 200 gems: 1.27. The heavier variant at offset -3 gives 1.17 (1.33 at 200 gems). The old x1.4 is above all of them. A player can check the inputs on screen: the base pay on the card, the price on the Summon button, the tag's multiplier, and the join line with the squad HP that caused it.

FREQUENCY weight 8 (unchanged), not [duel], trial false. Under the u-honesty draw rule (chance = odds x weight / 66) with the three live rows: 2.4 / 3.5 / 5.0 / 8.2% of contracts at levels 1 / 5 / 10 / 20; at least one on a 5-contract board 11 / 16 / 23 / 35%. With all nine rows live (cap binds): 2.1 / 3.2 / 4.7 / 7.9%.
approvedDesign.playerEffect: Before launch the brief shows one extra row (species, level, x1, "follows the squad", HP when the town has met it). The decision is the 70% line, and it is made during the run. Below 70% average HP between fights the squad has three choices: rest, since REGEN returns 0.5% of max HP per second (60 s of walking is 30 points) and in-fight healing and potions are already counted when the fight ends; keep going, in which case the next fight that opens gets an elite-tier fighter added; or order a retreat, which ends the follower's joins at once. Before the terms are met the order costs the contract. After the terms are met it costs nothing, because the verdict reads the terms before the withdrawal flag, and 40 of the 68 measured joins were in that walk home. A squad that never retreats and never rests below the line paid 0.500 vs 0.386 deaths per contract (+30%); a squad that orders the retreat at 70% paid +4% over the same policy without the twist and lost 1.5 wins per 100 contracts. A squad that stays above the line never sees the follower, and then the contract paid x1.15 for nothing. Composition matters for the rate: under the heavier variant two clerics cut the join rate from 34% to 25% of contracts. During the run the log prints the HP that triggered a join and the tally shows "1 following" while the follower is on the map. Killing the follower is possible only in the fight it joins.
approvedDesign.secondOrder: Retreat (u-retreat as built: sortie.js exitState, field.js contacted/retreat): the order gains a use it does not have today. In this harness the order at under 70% HP between fights cut deaths 21% with the follower and 4% without it. Releasing the follower does not close the free call-off (it is not spotted, field.js:1477). The squad's own break-off sheds the follower the same way as an order. Wounds (u-wounds): joins are the fights that end with the squad at its lowest, so they feed the lowest-HP trigger; deaths replace wounds for the squads that lose a member. Permanent death: 0.386 -> 0.500 deaths per contract (+30%), 1.4 deaths per join, 28 joins per 900 contracts while the squad is still working. Tactics: tactics.js reads only side "theirs" (:209, :230, :250, :305), so the follower never counts as closing and cannot cause stand plays; the plan layer does not know the follower exists, so its odds readings understate a fight the follower will join. Chorokinetic: loneTarget (field.js:948) and the terror kit read isTheirs, so a wormhole cannot land on it; once it has joined, escapeHatch (:991) can break the fight off like any other. No resupply: the 70% line is crossed for good after the first big fight, so the join rate rises (26% to 33% of contracts under the heavier variant). Bestiary: look() records the species at first sight (noteSighting), so the first Hunted contract adds the species to the town's bestiary. Loot and kill counts: the follower is a normal kill once it has joined (+1 hostile for kill quotas). Overlap with Reinforcements: a body that takes a side at a fight and a group that arrives on a cue are different triggers; both can roll on one contract (max two twists) and their effects multiply.
approvedDesign.risks: All figures come from gearless squads of 4 without potions; absolute deaths are upper bounds and only the relative change is usable. The default has few events: 68 joins in 900 contracts, so the three seeds disagree more than for the other twists (+0.12, +0.19, +0.04); the heavier variant has 463 joins in 1800 and agrees (+0.17, +0.12, +0.15). One join costs 1.4 deaths because a level+1 elite arrives in a fight the squad is already losing. Most joins (40 of 68) are on the walk home after the terms were met, where the only lever is the free retreat order; a player who never uses the order meets the follower there. Choosing between the two gates is a design decision, not a tuning one: afterWithdraw false gives the retreat order a function and a lower, more variable cost; true gives +37% and an order that does not help (-4%). The 70% line is the engine's break-off average (field.js:1015) without the "someone down" clause. Hunted over Night is unmeasured for sight 5 beyond the pair above (the follower at 4 tiles is inside sight 5). The follower is not in the loadout plan unless pursuit-twist-plumbing item 6 lands. Needs u-honesty and pursuit-twist-plumbing first; fieldview.js, bestiary.js and sortie.js are being edited by wave 2 builds, so line numbers will move.
approvedDesign.response: Design attack, accepted in full: the join was the minority path (317 of 2478 follower fights) and the cost was a trailing elite met on the way out. The follower is now unengageable (side "neutral", combatant() false) and only the join remains; re-measured above. The demand was that it keep its distance when approached, reusing the quarry flee goal; I implemented the same guarantee differently because a flee goal needs a distance field from the squad's current position every step and a follower cornered in a dead end would fight anyway, while a one-line combatant() test gives "walking at it never opens a fight" as an invariant that test/contracts.js checks. Tactics.closing: verified, it reads side "theirs" only. The "leaving" statistic is split (126 / 54 / 524 baseline deaths) and the split changed the design: with the follower active on the walk out after a withdrawal, 74% of joins land on squads that are already breaking off and the retreat order is worth 4%, so the default stops the follower at withdrawal. Price: stated rule and inputs, x1.15 (x1.27 at 200 gems per death) against x1.25 for +0.16 deaths on Reinforcements; the x1.4 is gone. Two corrections to what I expected: the unengageable follower is MORE lethal than the fightable one at the same offset (+37% against +25% under the heavier variant), because the squad can no longer end the twist by killing it early; and with the withdrawal clause most joins (40 of 68) move to the walk home after the terms are met. quests.js trial threading is pursuit-twist-plumbing. Engineering attack, accepted: both respawn loops (plumbing item 5), tooltip names the measured cost, trial threading, price rule, one Hunted row only (Hunted B is dropped). Declined in form: building on a Reinforcements cue-spawn shape; I could not see that proposal. The cue used here is the existing TEMPORAL/cued mechanism (mapgen.js:45, field.js arrivals) that last-wave groups use, and the only new actor data is `keep`; no stance and no new goal branch except the one loop in chooseGoals. If Reinforcements lands an `arrive` shape, "trail" becomes one value of its `on`.

verdicts.attack: The card's idea, joining the fight going worst, is a minority path in the builder's own counters: the join fires in 14% of sorties and accounts for 58 of 533 follower fights; the cost comes from an elite standing on the route out that the squad walks into (54% of follower fights after leaving, 49 of 52 deaths in them). That is the same effect as reinforcements-a's column and hunted-b's pack, with a different trigger. A pre-spotted elite within NEAR 14 tiles counts as 'closing' for tactics every tick (tactics.js:224-231 reads a.spotted), so stand plays rose 0.22 to 0.36 against something that never attacks. The premise '76 of 100 deaths happen after the squad started leaving, the unthreatened part of a run' conflates two states: withdraw() (field.js:383) and leave() (field.js:1875) both set phase 'leaving', so that count includes squads already broken and running. x1.4 for +0.11 deaths against reinforcements-a's x1.25 for +0.16.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: TWISTS.hunted missiontypes.js:829 (weight 8, x1.4, not duel/arena; 'arena' is a map id); chooseGoals hostile loop :766-815 with GIVE_UP 20 :62; findSkirmishes ENGAGE 2 :1197 and openSkirmish resolving once :1219; hpOf :917 and escapeHatch's 0.7-with-someone-down rule :1013; fighterFor species rule sortie.js:133-136; nameCast :61; TEMPORAL mapgen.js:45; ACTOR_KEYS has no stance/joined :1943. quests.js:116 does NOT pass trial: true today (the proposal's parenthetical reads as if it did); it is a change the proposal must make. Scratchpad pursuit f_hbase_*/f_ha_* re-aggregated: 68.4%/0.251 to 65.8%/0.361 over 1800 paired sorties, exact match.
verdicts.demand: Make it a follower only: it keeps its distance when approached (reuse the quarry/flees goal so walking at it never opens a fight), is skipped by kill atoms and rally, and fights only through the join. Re-measure; the price is then for the join and the design is distinct from Reinforcements. Either exclude stance actors from Tactics.closing() or state the stands as intended. Split the 'leaving' statistic into after-leave() and after-withdraw() before using it as a premise. Thread the trial flag through quests.js:116 explicitly as a change.

verdicts.attack: Two respawn loops clone the follower. escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch of portalTick() (:1373-1376) iterate every hostile/patrol group in s.map.spawns with no deferred check; the follower's cast group (role hostile, count 1) is in that list, and makeActor reads g.follows, so a Hardcore escalation adds a second trailing elite and every window shut adds one more. reinforcements-a skips its arrive groups; neither hunted design mentions it. The mechanic the card describes is not what costs: the join fired in 14.1% of sorties, while the follower was in 533 fights over 450 sorties and 49 of its 52 deaths came after the squad started leaving, so the +44% is 'an elite stands on the route home' and the tooltip's 70% rule is decoration. quests.js:116 does not pass trial: true today (mt.roll(type, { level, name })) and roll() has no trial option, so the exclusion is three lines of threading, not a flag read. The follower keeps tactics.closing() (tactics.js:224) armed for the whole run (spotted and found, inside NEAR 14), which is the unexplained rise in stand plays. x1.4 is 'no formula'; under the terrain rule the inputs give about 1.19, under the arrivals rule about 1.24. Depends on u-honesty.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: row :829-830; GIVE_UP :62, HEADSTART :63, ENGAGE :55; chooseGoals hostile loop :766-815; findSkirmishes :1197-1217 and openSkirmish :1219 resolving once before the record exists; combat.js encounter :613; hpOf :917 and escapeHatch's down > 0 && avg < 0.7 at :1015; fighterFor :133/:136; nameCast :61; mapgen TEMPORAL :45 and deferred :340; ACTOR_KEYS :1943; brief :201-212. Scratchpad proj2 has stance 'trail', the recruit at openSkirmish with JOIN_RULE=hp, the release at 8 tiles, and the taskGoal/rally skips. Logs: hbase 70/69/67% and 0.21/0.27/0.28, ha 68/64/65% and 0.31/0.40/0.38, joins 85+79+89 = 253; the +44%, 65.8%, 0.361 and 253 joins reproduce; the sweep (veteran +5%, elite 0/-1/-2/-3: 0.52/0.42/0.34/0.31 against 0.21) reproduces from h_a_0.45, h_ae_0.45, h_aoff-1/-2/-3. Frequencies 2.4/3.5/5.0/8.2% match my live3-plus-row simulation (2.4/-/4.9/8.1), which is not the all-nine pool.
verdicts.demand: Skip follows groups in both respawn loops. Build the follower on the same cue-spawn mechanism as reinforcements (a spawn group with {on, from, stance}), not a parallel TEMPORAL/stance path. Make the tooltip state the cost that is measured (walks behind the squad and is met on the way out) or change the follower so it is not on the route home when it has not joined. Thread trial through roll() to rollTwists. Price with the agreed rule on test/sortie.harness.js. The overseer approves at most one of hunted-a and hunted-b.

sharedRules: Shared rules the user approved for every complication: (1) one price rule: the multiplier keeps expected gems per attempt equal, counting a death at PULL_COST (100 gems), R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x 100 / (p1 x W0), rounded up to the next 0.05; (2) every number is re-measured on test/sortie.harness.js (add TWISTS=, GEAR=1 options if missing), not on a private runner; (3) at most one body-adding complication per contract (reinforcements, hunted, trap, turncoat, infested) until pairs are measured; (4) log lines state what spawned, where, at what distance and which term changed, in the engineering register; (5) trial: false on every row that adds bodies, threaded through quests.js.

conflicts: Three pricing conventions for the same quantity. Terrain prices a death at PULL_COST 100 gems and rounds up to 0.05; arrivals prices it at 200 gems plus kill drops; pursuit uses the relative rise in deaths with no formula. Same-sized effects get different multipliers: hunted-a +0.11 deaths per run -> x1.4, reinforcements-a +0.16 -> x1.25, infested-a +0.14 -> x1.50, trap-a +0.012 -> x1.15, storm-a +0.03 -> x1.05. None of the multipliers is derivable by the player from anything on screen (numbers-must-be-traceable); the per-twist record all three propose as the check is specified three ways (gs.field.twists { sent, won, dead } in terrain and arrivals; 'u-ledger can add' in pursuit) and u-ledger part A defines only gs.field.types. One owner, one R stated as data, one record shape.

Exit-route stacking. reinforcements-a (column from the entry 45 s after contact), hunted-a and hunted-b (a body trailing the squad), trap-a (a mark at the way home) and turncoat-a (the ward at the far end) all add bodies to the walk out, where the pursuit lens measured most deaths already occur. rollTwists allows two twists per contract (missiontypes.js:863, max 2) and no proposal measured any pair; the multipliers multiply (1.25 x 1.4 = 1.75) while the deaths very likely compound. Hardcore pairs are treated four different ways (trap-a skips once escalated, reinforcements-a skips arrival groups in the escalation re-spawn, infested-b doubles the escalation re-spawn through the swollen count, storms scale the escape window) and none is measured.

hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same mechanism (a hostile group released behind the squad that reaches it on the way out); the pursuit builder says approve one. hunted-a's dominant effect (the squad bumps into a trailing elite) is the same mechanism again with one body.

Every proposal depends on u-honesty (MT.modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, TWIST_FULL, MT.factors, MT.payout), none of which exists in the code (grep finds no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, TWIST_FULL or MT.current in *.js). The mods fold table would carry about 15 keys with three fold semantics (multiply: move, damage, regen, sight; union/concat: noReach, status, arrivals; largest: promote; sum: swell; first: ambush, pit; plus follower/pack/turn/informant) and the pursuit rows add a cast: (lv) => [...] function on the TWISTS row that must never reach a saved mission. 'A twist is a table row plus one consumer' becomes a dispatch table; the fold rules need one owner and one test.

Field flags for 'a hostile that moves on its own trigger' are named four ways: march (reinforcements-a), stance 'trail' / 'pack' plus follows (hunted-a/b), spotted preset true (hunted), spottedAt (reinforcements-b); each adds ACTOR_KEYS entries and a chooseGoals branch. trapTick/ringTile are claimed by trap-a and trap-b and offered to Reinforcements. u-retreat's contacted() is edited by trap-a (adds s.trapped) and paralleled by reinforcements-a's contactAt; one definition of contact must serve the button, the column clock and the trap.

Frequency figures use different rules: terrain and pursuit quote u-honesty's odds x weight / 66; arrivals quotes today's rule with nine rows. With all rows live the legal pool exceeds 66 on every type (73 to 102 by weights proposed), so the honesty promise 'others unchanged until the weights sum to 66' fails slightly: by my exact two-draw calculation over the 16 types, at level 10 dry falls 6.5% to 5.9-6.1% and hardcore 5.5% to 5.0-5.2%. reinforcements-b (weight 24) and turncoat-a (weight 12) are weight hikes with no stated reason beyond compensating 'only'.

storm-a and storm-b are alternatives, but storm-b's bow rule changes every water-spell Wet outside storms (elements.js:170 is shared with spellcraft.js:54), while storm-a's lives only in combat.js; approving storm-b as written is a global balance change, approving storm-a is a twist-local special case. Both carry the same unpriced walking tax on window contracts.

Three private combat-backed runners (proto/exp/real.js, arrivals/run.js, pursuit/run.js) with three baselines (82.4%/0.10-0.115, 69.5%/0.258, 68.4%/0.251 deaths per run) that cannot be compared, while test/sortie.harness.js, the project's combat-backed harness (named in memory and in test/field.harness.js's header), was used by none; the terrain lens asks for 'a combat-backed runner in test/' that already exists.
missed: Trials. quests.js:116 rolls trial twists through MT.roll with no flag and no filter, so star trials, including the one-body solo road, draw every row. Only the pursuit lens adds trial: false, and it describes quests.js:116 as already passing trial: true, which it does not. Storm, Reinforcements (at least one extra body per written group against a single character), Infested and A trap on a solo trial are unmeasured and unexcluded.

The one-sided-fight quirk. sortie.js:158-160 gives noFightUntil = clock + 120 to every actor in a skirmish whose party or foes list is empty, so any hostile that catches a lone ward (no species, no fighter) is pacified for 120 in-game seconds. trap-a and turncoat-a both put a mark next to a ward, and nobody checked this path; it is also the reason 0 of 960 wards died, which the pursuit lens reports as a fact without the cause.

Phase 'leaving' is set both by withdraw() (field.js:383, a broken squad running) and by leave() (field.js:1875, the job done). The pursuit lens's premise that the walk out is 'the unthreatened part of a run' (76 of 100 deaths after leaving) counts post-withdrawal deaths; u-retreat's exitState reads s.withdrew and s.phase too. Any design that keys on 'the walk home' needs the two split.

The walking-speed term on window contracts. makePortal's shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1308); both storms scale only Hardcore's escape window, so escort and rescue (deadline true -> window) take the whole x0.8 tax: storm-b's own result file shows escort deaths 0.07 to 0.20-0.23 per run, unreported, and storm-a's shows rescue 0.07 to 0.12 from the move term alone.

Loadouts are planned once against a pseudoZone of species at mission level (missions.js:97-100 samples every species at mission.level; sortie.js:112 keys the cache by species count). infested-a's promoted third is fielded at level + 3 but planned against at mission level; storm-a/b and reinforcements-a patch the cache key, infested-a does not. missionProfile needs the fielded level per body or the brilliant-mind planning advantage the storm proposals claim does not exist for promoted casts.

Permadeath value. The user rates anything that prevents a death far above damage; all twelve proposals add deaths (+0.012 to +0.235 per run) and none adds a lever that prevents one. The only readable 'leave now' signals are reinforcements-a's countdown and hunted-a's HP gate. A complication whose counterplay is a death-prevention action (a window in which the retreat order is free again, a spotter kill that cancels an arrival the squad can see) would fit the stated values; none was proposed.

Register. Proposed log lines include 'The paper was wrong: <label> is here for them', 'The floor gives way', 'the pack closes in', 'come out of the dark', 'The informant left': narrative, not the mechanic and the number (ui-prose-engineer-style). Every new line should read like the existing 'Complications: Storm' and 'wave 2 of 4' lines: what spawned, where, at what distance, and which term changed.

Save compatibility of board offers. A held board offer or saved run rolled before the build carries a twist id whose row now has mods or a cast function; the pursuit lens stales such offers through MT.current, the arrivals lens does not (a saved 'reinforcements' contract pays x1.25 with no column until the board rerolls), and the terrain lens derives mods from mission.twists so old runs change behaviour mid-run on reload. One rule for 'an offer rolled under an older table' is needed across all rows.

No proposal measured on a real save with gear and potions (all say so) or with the two-twist pairs the board can roll; and no proposal gives the overseer a repeatable command in test/ that reproduces its headline numbers, which test/sortie.harness.js's OUT/diff mode already supports.

conflicts: Alternatives on one row: storm-a/storm-b, trap-a/trap-b, reinforcements-a/reinforcements-b, infested-a/infested-b, hunted-a/hunted-b each re-add the same TWISTS id with different mods keys, MOD_TEXT lines, weights and only/not lists; at most one per row can land, and the arrivals lens did not say so for its two pairs.

Three incompatible price rules. Terrain: R = p0/p1 + (d1 - d0) x PULL_COST(100) / (p1 x W0), no drops. Arrivals: m = (W0 F0 + L0 + 200 dd - L1) / (W1 F1), a death costs 200 and kill drops count. Pursuit: the measured relative rise in deaths, no formula. On the same inputs hunted-a is 1.19 (terrain rule), 1.24 (arrivals rule) or 1.4 (as proposed); turncoat-a at levels 1-4 is about 1.08 against 1.5; infested-a is 1.31 against 1.50; storm-a is 1.05 against about 1.10. u-honesty's MT.factors prints these multipliers side by side on one card, so the six rows must be priced by one rule.

Weight budget. u-honesty's draw rule is odds x min(1, poolWeight / TWIST_FULL) with TWIST_FULL = 66 and the promise that adding rows leaves the others unchanged 'until the weights sum to 66'. The original nine rows sum to 84; with the A variants the per-type pool is 75-87, with the B variants 64-96 (reinforcements-b 24, infested-b 13, turncoat-a 12), so the cap binds everywhere: my simulation (60000 rolls per level) has night 7.89% to 7.51%, dry 6.49% to 6.02%, hardcore 5.67% to 5.19% at level 10 under the A weights, and each lens computed its own frequency under a different pool (pursuit: three live rows plus its own; terrain: the same; arrivals: all nine on the current rule). One owner must set TWIST_FULL to the real total or rescale the weights.

Four cue-spawn mechanisms for one idea. reinforcements-a/b: cast groups with arrive {on, delay} and a fired flag in map.spawns, march stance, contactAt/spottedAt; hunted-a/b: TEMPORAL 'trail', cued(), counters.trailed, stance trail/pack with their own chooseGoals branches and taskGoal/rally skips; trap-a: springAmbush with ringTile and a mark; all walk a new hostile group onto the map on a cue and give it a goal rule. The axes memory asks for one mechanism with data ({on, delay, from, stance}) read by one spawner and one goal branch; the pursuit lens itself says the stance code 'should land once'.
hunted-b and reinforcements-a are the same effect (bodies arriving from the entry behind the squad) under two labels and two prices (x1.4 and x1.25); the pursuit lens says do not approve both.

Trial roads. hunted-a/b and turncoat-a/b add trial: false and a rollTwists filter; storm, trap, reinforcements and infested do not, so a one-body solo trial can roll Reinforcements, Infested or Storm. The claim that quests.js:116 passes trial: true is false today (mt.roll(type, { level, name }); roll() has no trial option), so whichever lands first must thread it.

u-retreat's contacted() is extended three ways: trap-a adds !!s.trapped, reinforcements-a mirrors it with s.contactAt set in look() and openSkirmish(), hunted pre-marks followers spotted to stay out of it; one definition of contact, in one place, before any of these.

MOD_TEXT shape. u-honesty specifies a static table keyed by mod; terrain and arrivals generate per-contract text (member lines, 'x bodies on this paper', species tags), so the honesty API must take (mods, mission) before these build; infested-b's and reinforcements-a's cards cannot be produced from the static table.

All three lenses say wave 1 is editing field.js, sortie.js, combat.js and missiontypes.js. Wave 1 is finished (.team-backup/r1w1, project files dated 01:xx-03:06); wave 2 started at 03:09 (.team-backup/r1w2) and holds u-honesty, u-retreat, u-wounds, u-ledger, u-readout and u-debrief, which touch every file these twelve cite. Every line number here moves before any of them builds, and none lists after: ['u-honesty', 'u-retreat'] in a form the scheduler reads.
missed: u-honesty is approved but not built: missiontypes.js has no modsOf, MOD_TEXT, MT.current, MT.factors or TWIST_FULL (grep across *.js is empty) and its spec moves the six rows out of TWISTS into a comment block. All twelve proposals write MODS entries against that API and re-add rows it removes; none states the dependency as a build order, and a builder landing before it would write a second, incompatible fold.

None of the three lenses used test/sortie.harness.js (u-harness, approved and present: boots game.html's script list through test/game.boot.js and plays real Sortie launch/skip/settle with combat.js, gear, potions, Condition pools and Outfit). Each wrote a private runner that re-implements resolve(), tick() regen and nameCast with gearless parties; every absolute death rate is an upper bound by the builders' own admission, and every multiplier is priced on those numbers. The field-balance-harness memory says to quote game figures from sortie.harness.js.

Storm and the window clock: escort, assassination, rescue, pursuit, sabotage and capture carry deadline: true (missiontypes.js:409, :524, :595, :618, :640, :708), exitFor (:195) gives them the window exit, and shutsAt is mission.duration (field.js:1313). Walking x0.8 shortens the usable window by 20% on six types; neither storm design scales or discloses it (only Hardcore's escalate seconds are scaled).

escalate() (field.js:1557-1560) and the window-shut branch (:1373-1376) respawn 50% / 30% of every hostile and patrol spawn group with no check for deferred, at, arrive or follows, so any twist that adds a cast group gets it cloned on escalation and on every window shut. reinforcements-a skips its groups; hunted-a and hunted-b do not.

Stale offers: boards re-roll every 6 minutes (sortie.js:97) but trial offers persist per character until the star changes (quests.js:112); any twist that changes the cast at roll time (reinforcements-a/b, infested-a/b, hunted-a/b) leaves already-rolled offers carrying the tag with no bodies behind it and the multiplier still applied. Only hunted-a proposes an MT.current cast check.

describe().hostiles (missiontypes.js:1047) sums hostile+patrol+mark counts in m.cast; the card's hostile figure includes a column or follower unless excluded. hunted-a excludes follows groups; reinforcements-a/b do not.

combat.js types a spell's main strike by strikes[0].type (:303) and its splash as 'arcane' (:308); storm-a's per-type damage multiplier misses heat splash. Riposte (:215) uses the target's damageType and DoT (:593) the condition's type, so those paths are covered.

trap-a sets s.doneAt = null at the spring; verdict() (field.js:1636) withdraws with 'this is going nowhere' when !s.withdrew && !s.doneAt && s.clock >= duration x ABANDON (2.5), so a late squad is pulled out at the moment the ambush appears.

The measured cost of hunted-a, hunted-b and part of reinforcements-a is a body on the route home (hunted-a: 49 of 52 follower-fight deaths after leaving; hunted-b: 84 of 86; reinforcements-a: 26% of firings after the walk home starts), while the tooltips describe triggers (HP under 70%, commit at 60%, contact + 45 s) that the builders' own sensitivity tables show barely move the outcome. Under the traceable-numbers rule the card has to name the thing that costs.

Positive levelOffset is new to the engine: SWARMED (field.js:84) clamps it to 0.15 and feeds makeActor hp/power (:1682-1683) and every odds() call tactics makes; infested-a includes the fix, but nothing else that reads levelOffset was audited for the sign (bestiary brief, noteSighting and castLevel add it correctly; the plain harness and tactics tests assume it is negative).

Perf was measured for one proposal only (infested-b: hostiles per run 13 to 24, 35 at level 8, Node only). turncoat-b puts an actor scan under found()/known() (10 call sites in field.js, several inside per-actor filters per step); trap-b rebuilds the map mid-run; reinforcements-b scans the whole tile grid once per call. None was timed in the browser.

Evidence slips that do not change verdicts but should be corrected in the specs: terrain's fire-word class list (classes.js has mastery 'fire' in grenadier :466, artillerist :566 and kineticist :999, not arcanist or elemental_mage; the picker line must come from Classes.lexiconOf at classes.js:1818, which the proposal does name); pursuit's 'quests.js:116 passes trial: true' (it passes level and name only); the 1950-run storm figures and all trap figures are not in any results file in the scratchpad (proto/out holds storm_random.txt at n=1500 with different death rates, storm_b_wet.txt and storm_b_cands.txt), while every pursuit log and the arrivals final-n100 files reproduce the quoted numbers.
